title: References, Aliasing, and Shared Data
learningObjectives: Explain the main concept in this lesson.
Identify how references, state, or lifetime affect behavior.
Trace an example and predict its result.
Choose an appropriate practice for a simple scenario.

understand.concept: References and aliasing mean more than one name or variable can access the same underlying data or object. Changes through one alias may be visible through another. A reference can avoid copying large data, but shared access needs careful reasoning. The exact reference model differs by language.
understand.whyItMatters: Aliasing explains unexpected changes, shared state, and why object copying requires deliberate choices.
understand.analogy: Two people share one notebook; edits by one are visible to the other. This does not model ownership or synchronization.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy simplifies software rules; language and runtime behavior may differ.

explain.narrative: Identify the data or resource, who can access it, and how it changes or remains available. Trace the example, and consider what happens after a function returns or when an error interrupts normal flow. Use language-specific lifecycle and ownership rules for real implementations.
